'''Marina Huerta''' (born 1968) is an Argentinian theoretical [[physicist]] and a physics professor. She is known for her work on quantum entropy in quantum field theory. She has provided a new interpretation of the [[Bekenstein bound]]. As of 2020, she has 29 peer-reviewed publications with more than 2000 citations.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://www.scopus.com/authid/detail.uri?authorId=7005841250|title=Scopus preview - Huerta, M. - Author details - Scopus}}</ref>

In 2015 she won the New Horizons in Physics - [[Breakthrough Prize in Fundamental Physics|Breakthrough Prize]]<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|title=Breakthrough Prize|url=https://breakthroughprize.org/|website=breakthroughprize.org|language=en|access-date=11 May 2020}}</ref> for "fundamental ideas about entropy in quantum field theory and quantum gravity".<ref>{{cite press release|title=Recipients Of The 2015 Breakthrough Prizes In Fundamental Physics And Life Sciences Announced|periodical=|publisher=|url=https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/recipients-of-the-2015-breakthrough-prizes-in-fundamental-physics-and-life-sciences-announced-282088991.html|url-status=|access-date=|archive-url=|archive-date=|last=The Breakthrough Prize|date=|year=|language=en|pages=|quote=}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Físicos galardonados volvieron a Bariloche con su In 2024 she was awarded the [[Dirac Medal (ICTP)]] jointly with her husband Horacio Casini, Shinsei Ryu and Tadashi Takayanagi.<ref>[https://www.ictp.it/home/dirac-medallists-2024 Dirac Medal (ICTP) She researches quantum field theory and quantum information at the Centro Atómico Bariloche and the Argentinian research organization: [[National Scientific and Technical Research Council|CONICET]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Staff|url=https://fisica.cab.cnea.gov.ar/particulas/staff.php?user=Huerta|website=fisica.cab.cnea.gov.ar|access-date=22 May 2020}}</ref> She is a professor at the [[Balseiro Institute|Instituto Balseiro]] of the Universidad Nacional de Cuyo in Argentina where her lectures on special relativity<ref>{{Cite web|title=Instituto Balseiro - Clases en linea|url=https://www.ib.edu.ar/academicas/clases-en-linea/item/1437-mecanica-clasica.html|last=|first=|date=|website=|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=}}</ref> have been filmed and are offered free of charge (in Spanish). The Strings School has published her lectures on entanglement entropy<ref>{{cite AV media| url-status = live| archive-url = https://ghostarchive.org/varchive/youtube/20211210/aB1P6lA2GAE| archive-date = 10 December 2021| url = https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=aB1P6lA2GAE| title = Entanglement Entropy - I by Marina Huerta | website=[[YouTube]]}}{{cbignore}}</ref> (in English).

== Biography ==
Marina Huerta was born in 1968 in Buenos Aires, Argentina. She studied at the Universidad de Buenos Aires (UBA) and then moved to the [[Instituto Balseiro]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Breakthrough Prize – Fundamental Physics Breakthrough Prize Laureates – Marina Huerta |url=https://breakthroughprize.org/Laureates/1/L70 |access-date=28 May 2024 |website=breakthroughprize.org |language=en}}</ref> She obtained her Ph.D. in physics in the year 2000 after completing a doctoral dissertation on an effective description of the Quantum Hall Effect under the supervision of Guillermo Zemba and Rafael Montemayor.<ref>{{Cite web|title=RRHH|url=https://fisica.cab.cnea.gov.ar/particulas/rrhh.php|website=fisica.cab.cnea.gov.ar|access-date=22 May 2020}}</ref>

In 2005 and then in 2014, she spent some time at Princeton's [[Institute for Advanced Study]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.sns.ias.edu/previous?group=physics |title=IAS |access-date=18 May 2020 |archive-date=21 November 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151121161251/http://www.sns.ias.edu/previous?group=physics |url-status=dead }}</ref> On the 2014 visit, Huerta researched entanglement entropy which enlightens aspects of quantum field theory inaccessible with any other approach.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Marina Huerta|url=https://www.ias.edu/scholars/marina-huerta|website=Institute for Advanced Study|date=9 December 2019|language=en|access-date=22 May 2020}}</ref>

She was one of the organizers of the workshop 'Quantum Gravity in the Southern Cone' in 2019.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Home - VIII Quantum Gravity in the Southern Cone|url=https://fisica.cab.cnea.gov.ar/QGSC-VIII/index.php|website=fisica.cab.cnea.gov.ar|access-date=18 May 2020}}</ref>

== Contributions to physics ==
{{BLP unsourced section|date=July 2020}}
Huerta's main contributions in theoretical physics are in geometric entropy in quantum field theory, holography, quantum gravity and quantum information theory. She uses interlacing entropy as an indicator of confinement and phase transitions. It is considered the natural order parameter for systems with topological order. Relative entropy's properties give rise to the Bekenstein dimension, energy levels in field theories and the generalized second law. She has provided a new interpretation of the [[Bekenstein bound]] using relative entropy and distinguishability of states.

== Selected publications ==
*''On the RG running of the entanglement entropy of a circle.'' In: ''[[:de:Physical Review|Physical Review]] D.'' Band 85, 2012, S. 125016
*''Towards a derivation of holographic entanglement entropy.'' In: ''[[:de:Journal of High Energy Physics|Journal of High Energy Physics]]'' (JHEP). 1105 (2011) 036
*''Entanglement entropy in free quantum field theory.'' In: ''[[:de:Journal of Physics|Journal of Physics]] A.'' Band 42, 2009, S. 504007, [[arxiv:0905.2562|Arxiv]]
*''A Finite entanglement entropy and the c-Theorem.'' In: ''[[:de:Physics Letters|Physics Letters]] B.'' Band 600, 2004, S. 142–150
